excerpt: Phiar built AI-powered augmented reality navigation for drivers on phones and in-car screens. Y Combinator lists it as acquired; reports name Google as the buyer.
content:
Phiar Technologies was a Bay Area startup that built augmented reality navigation for driving. Instead of a flat map, its software used a phone or in-car camera feed and drew directions directly onto the live view of the road, while its AI detected lanes, vehicles and other traffic in real time. Y Combinator's profile describes it as building the first AI-powered AR navigation driving software, running on smartphones and in-vehicle displays. According to a 2022 report republished by the Japanese tech outlet BRIDGE, its products were a Spatial-AI Engine and a Mobility AR Engine; it sold to businesses such as fleets, ran proof-of-concept tests with car makers including Nissan, and worked with partners such as Panasonic Automotive, Bosch, TomTom and HERE.

Phiar was founded in 2017 and went through Y Combinator's Summer 2018 batch. BRIDGE reported that its founders were Chen-Ping Yu, a computer vision researcher who had been a postdoctoral researcher at Harvard, and James Briscoe. In 2021 Gene Karshenboym, who had led Google's Android automotive platform, became CEO, and Yu moved to the board.

Funding

BRIDGE reported that Phiar raised a $2.5 million seed round from investors including Y Combinator, Norwest Venture Partners and Mayfield, and a $12 million Series A in September 2021 led by State Farm Ventures.

Acquisition

Phiar's Y Combinator profile now lists the company as acquired, and links to a December 2022 news headline saying Google acquired the startup; BRIDGE also reported the acquisition by Google in September 2022. We have not found an announcement from Google with terms, and none were reported. Phiar's former website, phiar.net, no longer resolves.

Pricing

Phiar sold its software to businesses and did not publish prices. It is no longer offered as a standalone product.

This page is based on Phiar's Y Combinator profile, BRIDGE's 2022 report and Phiar's GitHub account. Details of the acquisition beyond these reports are not public.
